field.label: Enabled
field.comment: Off by default. While this is No the cron jobs return immediately and no feed is generated or delivered, whatever the individual feeds say.

field.label: Products per Batch
field.comment: Products loaded, rendered and written per batch. Each batch costs a fixed number of queries no matter what this is set to, so raising it trades memory for fewer round trips. Lower it if generation exhausts PHP memory on a catalog with large descriptions.

field.label: Time Budget per Run (seconds)
field.comment: Wall-clock budget for one cron tick. When it is used up the run saves its position and continues on the next tick, so a catalog larger than a single cron window still finishes. Keep it comfortably below the PHP max_execution_time of your cron process.

field.label: Validate After Generation
field.comment: Check the generated feed against its own validation rules and record the findings. This is what turns a feed a marketplace silently rejects into one you can see is wrong.

field.label: Keep Run History (days)
field.comment: Older rows are pruned by the dispatcher cron.

group.label: Google Merchant Center
group.comment:
Needed only for feeds delivered through the Google Merchant API. Downloading a feed or sending it by FTP uses none of this.

Google's Content API for Shopping v2.1 shuts down on 18 August 2026 and its endpoints then return 410 Gone; this module targets the replacement Merchant API, so no migration is required.

field.label: Merchant ID
field.comment: The numeric Merchant Center account ID that owns the data sources. Settable per website or store view, so different store views can submit to different Merchant Center accounts.

field.label: Service Account Key File
field.comment: File name of the Google service-account JSON key, resolved inside var/magenx_feed/gmc/. Upload it there by SSH or deployment, not into pub/media — that directory is web-served and the key grants programmatic access to your Merchant Center account. Treat it exactly like a password.

group.label: Agentic Commerce (OpenAI / ACP)
group.comment: Seller facts the OpenAI product feed repeats on every row. Templates read them as {{ context.store.name }}, {{ context.store.url }}, {{ context.store.privacy_policy }}, {{ context.store.terms }}, {{ context.store.return_policy }}, {{ context.store.accepts_returns }}, {{ context.store.return_days }}, {{ context.store.checkout }}, {{ context.store.brand }} and {{ context.store.weight_unit }}. Set them per store view: each store view is its own feed.

field.label: Seller Name
field.comment: Shown to shoppers as who sells the item. Empty uses General → Store Information → Store Name, then the store view name. Never a placeholder: the feed rejects them.

field.label: Fallback Brand
field.comment: Used for products with no manufacturer value. Fill it only if you sell your own brand; leave it empty if you resell, so a missing brand is reported by validation instead of being filled with the wrong one.

field.label: Headless Storefront URL
field.comment: Base URL of the storefront shoppers actually use, including the locale segment, e.g. https://shop.example.com/en. The ACP mapping builds product links as <this>/product/<url_key>, the MagenX Commerce product route. Empty uses Magento's own product URL - wrong for a headless store, where Magento does not serve product pages.

field.label: Return Window (days)
field.comment: Exported only when returns are accepted.

field.label: Offer Checkout in ChatGPT
field.comment: Sets is_eligible_checkout. Turn on only once OpenAI has enabled checkout for your integration and the storefront's /api/acp checkout is live (ACP_ENABLE=1 with Stripe configured). The flag alone does not enable checkout.

field.label: Recipient Email
field.comment: Leave empty to use the General Contact address.

field.label: Failure Email Template
field.comment: Sent through Magento's own Mail Sending Settings — this module configures no transport of its own.

group.label: Cron
group.comment: These jobs run in Magento's default cron group on purpose. A dedicated group is never picked up on hosts that run cron:run --group= with an explicit list, which makes feeds silently stop generating while the CLI command still works perfectly by hand.

field.label: Generation Dispatcher Schedule
field.comment: Cron expression. This is not the schedule a feed generates on — each feed carries its own days and times, and this dispatcher only ticks and decides which are due. It must therefore run at least as often as your finest per-feed time granularity.

field.label: Delivery Retry Schedule
field.comment: Cron expression for retrying deliveries that failed.
